_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Automatic Test Equipment (ATE) Interface Hardware Manual
summary: Provides format and content preparation instructions for the ATE Interface Hardware Manual, used to support installation, operation, and maintenance of automatic test equipment interface hardware.
use_relationship:
The ATE Interface Hardware Manual is used to support installation, operation, and maintenance of interface hardware for automatic test equipment.  This manual is directed toward technicians trained in the use of automatic test equipment to perform piece-part fault isolation.

This Data Item Description (DID) contains the format and content preparation instructions for the data product generated by the specific and discrete task requirement as delineated in the contract and paragraphs 4-2.b(8), 4-2.c, and 5-3.f of DS-56, Data Standard for the Preparation of INFOSEC Technical Manuals.

This DID is applicable to manuals prepared specifically for the Government.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Reference Documents
preparation_instructions.content: The applicable issue of the documents cited herein, including their approval date and dates of any applicable amendments, notices, and revisions, shall be as stated herein.  DS-56, Data Standard for the Preparation of INFOSEC Technical Manuals, current edition, are available at the National Security Agency, 9800 Savage Rd, Suite 6718, Fort Meade, Md 20755-6718, Attn: I8222.

preparation_instructions.title: Format
preparation_instructions.content: The test program manual information that is computer generated shall be provided on CDROMs.

preparation_instructions.title: Content
preparation_instructions.content: The front cover (handling instructions), Summary of Content page, Record of Amendments page, Table of Contents, List of Illustrations, List of Tables and Introduction, will be prepared by the Government at the time of final publication and are not deliverable items in accordance with this DID.  The manual shall contain six chapters as described in DS-56, "Data Standard for the Preparation of INFOSEC Technical Manuals", and outlined below.

children.title: Chapter 1: Description of ATE interface hardware
children.content: Describe the ATE interface and its purpose, and include the following:

children.title: The nomenclature and classification of the ATE interface
children.content: Include test head adapter, matrix boards, probe boards, plug-in elements, ancillary units and a short explanation of reference designations.

children.title: A general description of the purpose and function of the ATE interface
children.content: including a description of the electrical capabilities.

children.title: A brief physical description of the ATE interface
children.content: including a table of sizes and weights.

children.title: A photograph (three quarter view) of the complete equipment
children.content: with the accessories furnished by the manufacturer, and with major assemblies of the equipment identified.

children.title: Illustrations showing the position and identity of each plug-in unit, package, board, module, and chassis
children.content: (including a table listing titles, part numbers, and reference designations).

children.title: Chapter 2: Inspection
children.content: Provide instructions for unpacking, inspection, and preparing the equipment for reshipment.  Also include the following information:

children.title: Step-by-step procedures necessary to prepare the ATE interface for initial use.
Instructions for preliminary mechanical adjustment/alignment.
Procedures for repacking the equipment for reshipment
children.content: including disassembly or dismantling procedures, and requirements for special handling.

children.title: Chapter 3: Operating Procedures
children.content: Provide instructions to inform test station operators how to connect, adjust, and use the ATE interface hardware.

children.title: Chapter 4: Principles of Operation
children.content: Provide a general description of overall ATE interface operation.  Special emphasis shall be placed on electrical operation of any circuitry within the ATE interface.

children.title: Chapter 5: Corrective Maintenance
children.content: Provide corrective maintenance data, including the following:

children.title: A list of necessary tools and text equipment.
A procedure for trouble shooting the ATE interface.
children.content: This description should reference specific tests within the stimuli test of the ATE test program, and relate those tests to specific circuits within the ATE interface.

children.title: Additional test procedures, other than the stimuli test of the ATE Test Program
children.content: which are necessary to isolate the trouble.

children.title: Detailed disassembly procedures, if necessary, to gain access to or remove assemblies.
A procedure for repair of the ATE interface
children.content: including specific procedures and techniques.  Supporting illustrations, as necessary, shall also be included.

children.title: Timing, schematic, and wiring diagrams.
children.content: Timing diagrams should relate to the actual signals that are being processed in the stimuli test of the ATE test program.  The schematic diagrams should be the same as that used in the test program manual.

children.title: Chapter 6: Replaceable Parts
children.content: This chapter shall include a Group Assembly Parts List (GAPL) for each plug-in assembly and chassis assembly, including those parts mounted on panels, cases, covers, etc.  The Government will provide the GAPL.  The contractor shall provide parts location illustrations, as required, to support the GAPL for location and identification of all parts included in the GAPL (see paragraph 5-3.f of DS-56).

children.title: Security Classification
children.content: It is anticipated that the security classification of the interface hardware manual will be UNCLASSIFIED.  Unclassified manual will be marked FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY (FOUO).

children.title: Illustrations
children.content: Illustrations shall be prepared in accordance with paragraph 4-2.b(8) of DS-56, Data Standard for the Preparation of INFOSEC Technical Manuals.

children.title: Block Diagrams
children.content: Block diagrams shall contain the functional units of the ATE interface, and be drawn as rectangles enclosing the names given to the functions performed.  Block diagrams show the relationship of the functions to each other by interconnecting lines.  Simplified block diagrams will show only the major functional units.  A detailed block diagram will show all the functions within each block of a simplified block diagram.  If a block diagram is spread over two or more sheets, interconnections between sheets shall be clearly indicated.

children.title: Equipment Logic Diagrams
The reference designation of each circuit board shall be included on these diagrams.
Show the schematic type representations of R-C networks, filters, etc.
children.content: The component reference designation and value shall be shown (R1, 10K; C1, 10pf) and the type of module.

children.title: The logic diagrams shall list the names of all input or output signals to or from the ATE interface
children.content: the pin numbers to which they are applied, or from which they are taken, and their origins or destinations.  If a logic function is spread over two or more sheets, interconnections between sheets shall be clearly indicated.

children.title: All test points, plugs, receptacles, and pin numbers shall be shown and identified by reference designation.
Major logic functions shall be identified by name in a larger size type immediately adjacent to the circuitry for those functions.
Schematic Diagrams
children.content: The requirements identified in paragraph 4-2.c of DS-56 also apply to schematics.

children.title: Timing Diagrams
children.content: Timing diagrams shall show a sequence of operations and interrelationships.  These shall be graphic presentations in which a change of state is plotted against time and should relate to the actual signals being processed in the stimuli tests in the ATE test programs.

children.title: Wiring Diagrams
children.content: Wiring diagrams (or complete wire lists, including source and destination) shall show the connections between the ATE tester, all plug-in wiring boards, lamps, switches, etc.

children.title: Parts Location Illustrations
children.content: Parts location illustrations shall show the location of all parts for each ATE interface including those parts mounted on panels, cases, covers, etc.  Each part shall be identified either by reference designations or by find number in a manner that will facilitate correlation between the GAPL and the parts location illustrations.  If possible, the parts location illustrations shall be reproducible copies of the appropriate assembly drawings modified to remove notices, dimensions, find numbers and leader lines for non-maintenance items, and other such details that are not required for location and identification of parts included in the GAPL.  These requirements may necessitate preparing additional views as required for clarity.

children.title: Location of Illustrations
children.content: When possible, page-size and smaller illustrations shall be located on pages facing the text/tabular pages that make the first reference to them, or as soon as practicable following the first reference.  All foldout illustrations shall be grouped at the rear of the manual and shall be assigned numbers prefixed with the letters "FO-" followed by a dash and the figure number.  The foldout illustrations shall be assigned figure numbers consecutively beginning with "FO-1" for the first, FO-2 for the second, etc.  All sheets of a multiple sheet illustration shall be assigned the same figure number, with the individual sheets identified in parentheses following the figure title.

children.title: Engineering Drawings
children.content: If engineering drawings, schematics, etc., being prepared on the same contract fulfill the basic requirements, they shall be used in the manual.  Cost for these drawings, except for reproduction expense, should not be applied to this data item.
